title: Customize Order Lifecycle Safely
readerIntent: Implement customer policy and integrations through Nodics extension layers without forking core.
priorKnowledge: Understand Nodics module load order, services, Pipelines, Workflows and backend metadata.
owner: Customer project module layers after product modules
summary: Configuration-first overrides cover policy and selection; replace services, Pipeline nodes or Workflow definitions only when behavior truly differs, while preserving domain authority.

sections.heading: Configuration first
items: Layer cancellation windows and reasons under order.orderLifecycle policy and cancellationEligibility.
Layer Return windows, evidence, authorization and non-refundable dispositions without moving RMA or Inventory authority.
Layer Refund approval rules, exact thresholds and maker-checker requirements; keep amount strings exact.
Layer event-to-template audiences and provider service selection. Credentials remain secret references owned by the provider module.

sections.heading: Service and Pipeline extension
items: A later project module may replace the registered service name while retaining its public operation contract.
Override one Pipeline node to add customer validation or routing; preserve error handling, idempotency and the owner service call.
Use Workflow for human review, waiting, escalation and compensation. Use Pipeline for bounded synchronous technical steps.
Never wrap a Facade or service merely to create indirection. Override the closest stable extension point needed by the customer behavior.

sections.heading: Axis customization
items: Publish schemas, safe fields, help, filters and state actions from the backend capability catalogue.
Axis reusable Workbench components render the effective contract. A customer may extend presentation components, but must not encode approval, eligibility, provider or orchestration rules in Axis.
Permission removal must remove both navigation and actions; hiding a button alone is not authorization.

sections.heading: Partner verification
items: Test the effective layered configuration and prove core configuration remains unchanged.
Run persisted owner-boundary journeys for full, partial, duplicate, timeout, stale revision and recovery paths.
Qualify real payment and carrier adapters with production-like accounts, readiness, timeout, retry, webhook signature, idempotency, monitoring and reconciliation evidence.

sections.heading: AI coding contract
items: Inspect module ownership and existing extension points before adding files.
Prefer named exported operations and direct Facade-to-service delegation. Use a shared invoke helper only when callback and Promise adaptation is genuinely shared.
Document configuration keys, safe override examples, invariants, tests and operational consequences in canonical and module-local contracts.
